subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` defaults be allowed to override stricter later operator exec config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current docs and tests encode durable per-session `/exec` defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Clamp to current operator policy
options.body: Treat global or agent exec config and approval policy as an upper bound, then clear or clamp stored session exec fields that exceed it with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep durable session overrides
options.body: Preserve the current contract and document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Ship reset or doctor first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair path before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp to current operator policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec config and approval policy as an upper bound, then clear or clamp stored session exec fields that exceed it with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced the `/exec` session override behavior and owns the clearest history trail for the resolver/tests that would define the permanent contract.
